label: Photographic composition
description: Ways to arrange subjects, lines, shapes, depth and empty space within a photographic frame.
notes: Spatial arrangements within a single photographic frame belong here. camera.angle owns camera viewpoint, camera.shot_size owns framing distance, and camera.genre owns the photographic use or shooting convention. Values are noun phrases that follow “composed with”; lighting and color appear only where needed to define an arrangement, such as a silhouette or a reflection. This closed list favors visibly distinct structures over alternate names for the same composition.

values.look: The main subject sits near a third-line intersection, with the horizon often on a horizontal third.
The subject sits on the centerline, with matching shapes or masses on either side.
Roads, rails or other strong edges guide the eye through the frame toward the subject.
A small subject is surrounded by a broad, quiet area of sky, wall or another nearly empty surface.
A doorway, window or other complete opening encloses the main subject inside the photograph.
Curving forms lead inward along a tightening spiral toward an off-center focal point.
The main forms run on a strong slant across the image, giving the frame directional energy.
Nearby branches, curtains or rocks partly border the view, placing the subject beyond them.
Distinct foreground, middle-ground and background elements overlap to create a sense of distance.
The image contains only a few simple forms, with distracting textures and secondary objects stripped away.
The subject occupies almost the entire image, leaving little surrounding background visible.
A narrow strip of ground sits below a large expanse of sky.
Ground or water occupies most of the image beneath a narrow strip of sky.
Water, glass or a mirror visibly doubles the subject, building the arrangement around the reflected image.
A dark, readable outline stands against bright sky, with little detail inside the subject.
Similar windows, objects or forms repeat across the frame in a visible rhythm.
Three or five main elements form a group without splitting into equal pairs.
Three prominent points or forms define a stable triangle, directing attention around its corners.
Repeated forms radiate outward from one central point like spokes or petals.
A winding path, river or body line snakes through the frame in a loose S shape.
One large form on one side is balanced by several smaller forms or a strong accent on the other.
Important forms are cut by the image edges, making their continuation outside the frame part of the design.
A small familiar figure or object sits beside something much larger, making the size difference unmistakable.
The subject is anchored close to one corner, leaving the frame to extend mainly in the opposite direction.
Broad parallel strips of land, water, architecture or color divide the image into stacked layers.
